clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old male presented with sudden-onset expressive and receptive dysphasia, mild confusion, and right arm incoordination (NIHSS 5). Initial CT brain was normal, and he received thrombolysis for suspected ischemic stroke. Symptoms resolved within 2 hours. An admission nasopharyngeal swab for SARS-CoV-2 was negative. On day 3, new neurological symptoms including right arm weakness, dysphasia, amnesia, headache, vomiting, and pyrexia (39.7°C) developed, despite a normal MRI brain. A lumbar puncture on day 4 revealed inflammatory CSF with pleocytosis (134 x 10^6/L white cells, 99% lymphocytes) and elevated protein (0.52g/L). CSF PCR was positive for SARS-CoV-2 RNA (E gene CT 35.8, S gene CT 35.7), while other CSF tests for bacterial and common viral pathogens (HSV, VZV, enterovirus, parechovirus) were negative. An MRA on day 5 showed an incidental finding. Despite initial persistence of pyrexia and amnesia, the patient made a full recovery and was discharged by day 8. A follow-up MRI brain on day 25 was normal.
